title: Company All-Hands — Q2 FY26 Leadership Update
summary: Leadership reviewed Q1 metrics, product roadmap priorities (Dedicated, Private, Console features), hiring and org changes, compliance progress (SOC 2/ISO), and a prioritized list of company-level next steps. Town-hall style Q&A covered pricing, dedicated capacity SLAs, and upcoming benchmarks.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-28 17:00 PT — duration approx 60 mins — All Hands (Leadership update)
Attendees: Avery Cole (CEO); Maya Patel (CTO); Jordan Lee (Head Eng); Priya Rao (Head Product); Luis Martinez (Head People); Tess Nguyen (Head Revenue); ~120 employees on call (muted)

[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I want to kick us off, quick framing — overall Q1 we saw strong usage growth, we hit most of our reliability targets, but cost per token is still top of mind. We'll run through product, hiring, and security then open to Q&A.

[00:25] Maya: Quick note from infra — we've seen the new kernel selection landing in prod reduce p95 latency on mid-size seqs by about 12%, though there are some outliers on longer sequences. We're rolling a patch for the KV cache eviction logic, some of the telemetry was slightly off.

[01:05] Jordan: yeah, and the patch affects batching heuristics too; it's a small change but should help CPU spike behavior during bursts. Important: we need to coordinate Dedicated cluster upgrades with customers on reserved pools to avoid SLA blips.

[01:40] Priya: On product, roadmap highlights: Dedicated improvements (autoscaling policies and burst capacity), Private control plane GA timeline, and Console UX for per-route cost drilling. We're prioritizing autoscaling policies because customers asked for predictable tail latency with minimal waste.

[02:15] Tess: From revenue, we closed two mid-market contracts for Dedicated reserved capacity, both signed with 12-mo commits. This validates the reserved model. We need crisp docs around burst pricing and overage behavior, customers keep asking about latency vs cost tradeoffs.

[03:02] Luis: Hiring update — we're green to hire 18 net new engineers across runtime, infra, and a small product research team. We also are prioritizing Site Reliability hires to support Dedicated and Private. We'll post JD links later today.

[03:28] Avery: Quick finance: burn is in plan, runway's healthy after Series C; our focus is improving unit economics. Short term: the Optimize toolkit (intelligent batching, quant profiles) will be a leaver to lower token cost for customers.

[04:05] Maya: On Private — we've completed the initial KMS/HSM integrations and a handful of early customers are running internal pilots. Caveat: networking support (some older on-prem firewalls) required a few manual tweaks; we'll ship a more automated NAT traversal guide.

[04:40] Priya: For Console, the timeline for per-route token costing and a token-level latency heatmap is Q2 end for beta. Beta will go to existing Dedicated customers first.

[05:10] Staff question (via chat): Will you open the Private on-prem package to self-hosted GC?

[05:22] Maya: Short answer: yes, that's in scope but depends on packaging and support model. We expect to offer a hardened on-prem bundle with audit logs and an air-gapped installer in H2.

[05:40] Avery: Security/compliance — SOC 2 readiness is progressing, the auditors are scheduled for May; ISO shell work ongoing. We have a checklist in the security channel. My ask: engineering leads, please complete the control evidence tasks by next Monday.

[06:05] Jordan: We'll also add more tracing hooks into the runtime to make failure analysis faster — small perf cost but big reliability gains.

[06:40] Tess: A note on pricing and competition — customers are asking about comparisons to the large incumbents; our angle remains predictable economics and private deployment. We should tighten the messaging around performance per dollar.

[07:12] Employee question: What about model fallbacks and graceful degradation?

[07:23] Maya: We have automatic smart routing that can fallback to lower-cost variants; for hosted API it's enabled by default, Dedicated customers can opt-in. We'll publish the default policy and config knobs.

[07:55] Priya: Another product point — we're investing in eval tooling that ties regressions to prompt sets so we can prevent quality dips on quantized models. This is part of Redwood Optimize roadmap.

[08:30] Luis: People update — we launched the new comp bands; please review MyHR for changes. Also, all managers should schedule 1:1 calibration meetings next week.

[09:00] Avery: Ok, a couple of tough questions on plan: 1) Are we going to prioritize Dedicated scale above hosted feature parity? 2) Where do we draw the line for enterprise-only features?

[09:20] Priya: We plan a dual-track: core API parity stays first, but Dedicated/Private roadmap will have focused items around autoscaling, SLAs, and observability that are enterprise-centric. We'll avoid blocking hosted product progress — it's about prioritization.

[10:00] Tess: To add, enterprise go-to-market will include starter packages: reserved 3-month pilot and a technical onboarding bundle. That should lower friction.

[10:30] Employee question: Is there a hiring freeze?

[10:40] Luis: No freeze; we prioritized roles and have approvals. We will be conservative with IC vs management hires.

[11:05] (transcription hiccup) Speaker 3: "...we're seeing some ver... version skew in the internal J(??) —"

[11:28] Jordan: that's the KV cache mismatch I mentioned earlier — a small bug in the evict window, it can cause slightly higher memory under certain sequences. Patch inbound.

[12:00] Priya: Roadmap deep dive — dedicated autoscaler: goals are predictable p95 under 250ms for small models and 2nd-tier seqs, and provide a default burst policy that buys extra GPUs for short windows.

[12:40] Maya: The autoscaler will use workload-aware batching stats and compile-time kernel hints; it'll choose quantization-friendly kernels when cost is prioritized.

[13:10] Employee question (chat): Will the burst capacity be billed differently?

[13:20] Tess: Yes, burst is billed as metered added capacity; pricing will be additive to the reserved commit, but we'll include clear calculators in Console.

[13:55] Avery: We want to avoid surprises — UI should show projected spend for the month with bursts applied. Priya, please make that a priority for the beta.

[14:15] Priya: noted. We'll add a per-route forecast line item in the next Console beta.

[14:40] Security question: Where are the audit logs stored for Private?

[14:48] Maya: Private ships with option to push audit logs to the customer's S3 and to the control plane (if allowed). For air-gapped, we provide a local audit collector with secure export. Some early wording in security docs was ambiguous — we'll clar that.

[15:20] Employee: any update on regression incidents from last week?

[15:28] Jordan: root cause: an optimizer flag that changed kernel torch path selection — caused a subset of models to degrade on long sequences. Reverted the flag; regression has been mitigated and we'll run targeted evals.

[16:00] Avery: quick shout to ops — thanks for covering the incident. We should continue to instrument unit economics so we can tie customer outcomes to infra choices.

[16:25] Priya: on evaluations — we're rolling out a shared prompt-set repo where product, research, and SEs can add benchmark cases. The goal is to catch regressions early.

[17:00] Q&A open floor — lots of chat q's about docs, pilot eligibility, and benchmarking.

[17:35] Employee (verbal): How do we measure success for Private?

[17:42] Avery: success metrics are uptime SLA, deployment time, and customer-reported latency and cost. We'll agree on an SLO dashboard for each pilot.

[18:10] Priya: For GA readiness we need two pilot customers with production traffic and an ops runbook. Jordan, Maya — let's pick internal owners.

[18:36] Jordan: I'll own the runbook with Maya as technical lead, ETA first draft 2026-05-10.

[19:05] Tess: Sales playbooks — we'll create templates for pilot statements of work and a checklist for security artifacts.

[19:28] Luis: People ops — reminder about manager calibration and a new mentorship pairing program going live next week.

[20:00] Closing summary (Avery): recap — ship the roadmap doc (Priya), show Dedicated benchmarks (Maya), hiring plan (Luis), runbook for Private (Jordan). We'll share the slides and recording. Please ask follow-ups in the All Hands thread. Thank you.

[20:40] (end of formal remarks — open social Q&A, many attendees dropped but ~60 stayed for live questions)

Notes on transcription quality: moderate — a few names and acronyms mistranscribed; some crosstalk flagged as 'Speaker 3'.

Referenced artifacts: "Q1 metrics deck" (link posted in chat), "Dedicated perf spreadsheet" (to be shared), "Private pilot runbook (doc)" (link TBA).

Explicit next steps recap: Priya to publish roadmap by 2026-05-04; Maya to share benchmark sheet by 2026-05-07; Jordan to deliver Private runbook draft by 2026-05-10; Luis to post hiring plan by 2026-05-01.

End of transcript.
